info.title: Nabda — phone-owned SMS API
info.description: Nabda delivers a command to your own Android phone; the phone stores its queue and sends through your SIM. This specification describes the implemented free-edition control plane. It does not offer a carrier transport service, webhook delivery endpoint, push configuration API or bulk/campaign endpoint. A 202 response means accepted, not sent or delivered. Platform quotas differ from Android throughput and SIM costs. Bodies are limited to 131,072 bytes. Management routes use a verified GitHub sign-in and a Nabda browser session; third-party apps and phones use different Bearer credentials.

get.description: A successful response does not prove a phone is connected or an SMS was delivered.

post.summary: Accept one message command for a linked phone
post.description: Returns 202 only after durable cloud acceptance. The phone owns execution after handoff. Temporary recipient/text storage is purged after successful ACK. Sending is asynchronous; this response is not a send or delivery confirmation. At most 1,000 new commands/workspace/UTC day and 500 pending handoffs. No carrier cost is included. Use sandbox=true for tests.

post.summary: Fetch commands to stage in the phone database
post.description: An active phone receives at most 25 unacknowledged commands. Commands may repeat. Persist each command transactionally before ACK; polling does not authorize SMS. Cancel commands are prioritized. Expired unhanded commands are marked expired and their payloads removed during polling. Baseline idle interval is 60 seconds; FCM push is not configured by this API.

post.summary: Acknowledge durable storage and request execution handoff
post.description: Call only after SQLite commit on the phone. Only IDs returned in acknowledged may become execution-eligible. Cancellation/expiry between poll and ACK rejects that send. A legitimate earlier ACK repeats idempotently if its response was lost. Handoff clears cloud recipient/text. Acknowledging a cancellation command records receipt, not successful cancellation.

post.description: The message must already be handed off. Retransmit the same event ID and contents until it appears in accepted. Conflicting reuse, including within a batch, is rejected. Status is merged monotonically; stale queued events cannot regress sent/delivered. Late results may resolve outcome_unknown. The endpoint reports device claims, not independently verified carrier delivery.

ApplicationKey.description: Workspace application key, issued once by the dashboard and stored as a SHA-256 verifier. Cannot poll or impersonate a phone.

DeviceToken.description: Phone-only token returned by pairing. Cannot create messages or manage a workspace.

NabdaBrowserSession.name: __Host-nabda_session
NabdaBrowserSession.description: Opaque HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax Nabda session after top-level GitHub OAuth sign-in at /auth/github. The server verifies state, browser binding and S256 PKCE. The dashboard stays on the API origin. POST /auth/logout revokes this browser session. API keys and device tokens do not authenticate management calls; caller-provided identity headers are ignored.

message.description: A readable explanation and recovery hint.

status.description: sent and delivered are reports from the phone, not independent carrier attestations. Missing reports do not establish failure.

sandbox.description: A sandbox command must never invoke the phone's SmsManager.

cancellation_requested.description: The phone may not have received or completed this request yet.

device_id.description: An active phone in the authenticated workspace.

to.description: International E.164 or Libyan mobile local form. Arabic digits, spaces, parentheses and ASCII hyphens are normalized.

content.description: Preserved exactly, including whitespace. Must contain a non-whitespace character. The implementation checks at most 4,000 UTF-16 code units; emoji may consume two units.

sandbox.description: Set true for protocol testing without real SMS. This flag is durably included in the phone command.

send_at.description: Optional start time, including timezone. At most 30 days ahead; a past time becomes immediately eligible. Scheduling is executed on the phone.

expires_at.description: Latest permitted start time, including timezone. Must be later than send_at and now, within 31 days. Defaults to 24 hours after the later of now or send_at. This is not a recall deadline for an already submitted SMS.

guaranteed.description: True only when cancelled before durable phone handoff. After handoff, wait for the phone's result.

accepted_commands.description: New accepted platform commands today. This is not a count of successfully transmitted SMS.

reported_sent_messages.description: Messages created today with sent/delivered status reported by the phone.

reported_sent_parts.description: Sum of reported sent parts for those messages.

carrier_cost.description: The API cannot infer the mobile carrier's bill.

connected.description: Active credential with a heartbeat younger than 180 seconds. Connected does not by itself establish SMS readiness.

prefix.description: Display prefix only; the secret cannot be recovered.

key.description: Shown once. Keep it on your server; do not embed it in browser code.

pairing_token.description: Single-use token valid for ten minutes; keep the QR private.

counts.description: Counts across all messages in this workspace, not just this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor, or null. It preserves creation order, not a snapshot of mutable message status.

device_token.description: Shown once; protect with Android Keystore. This token cannot create application messages.

payload.description: message.send includes all fields; message.cancel uses an empty object. The phone must durably stage this before ACK and must not submit SMS until ACK approves the command ID.

event_id.description: Stable per-device ID. Retries must use identical event contents.

parts_total.description: When provided, must be 1–100 and cannot change after first reported.

parts_sent.description: Requires parts_total and must not exceed it.

parts_delivered.description: Requires parts_total and parts_sent; cannot exceed parts_sent.

failure_code.description: Symbolic diagnostic only. Do not include SMS text or recipient data.

DeviceEvent.description: sent requires parts_sent=parts_total; delivered requires all three part counters equal. A missing delivery report is not proof of failure. outcome_unknown must not trigger blind resubmission.

accepted.description: Only these events may be removed from the phone's durable outbound-event queue.

x-privacy.cloud_payload: Recipient and content are temporary command data until successful durable-phone ACK; they are then permanently removed from the cloud command. Message metadata and hashes remain.
x-privacy.expiry_cleanup: Expired commands are cleaned when the phone polls. This edition does not claim an exact scheduled deletion deadline.
x-privacy.phone_owned: SQLite owns recipient, body, queue, attempt and part history. No automatic lost-phone backup/restore is implemented.
